title: Cohort-sampler batching postmortem + field notes
content:
Summary:

This note captures the cohort-sampler batcher experiment we ran 2029-09-28 -> 2029-10-01, the regressions we observed in p99/p999, hypotheses we iterated on, and concrete next steps. The experiment combined a new cohort-sampler queuing discipline with adaptive microbatch sizing and a tightened KV-cache eviction threshold. Goal was to reduce average tokens-per-GPU while keeping 95th/99th latency under the SLO for medium-length chat (<= 1024 tokens).

Key outcomes (high level):
- Improved median token-cost by ~12% on the synthetic mixed-chat workload.
- p95 close to target (under 220ms per-token for 512-step bursts) but p99 regressed for high-concurrency cohorts (up to +18% on baseline).
- Two primary root causes identified: (1) cohort fragmentation leading to very small microbatches for long-tail request shapes; (2) increased KV eviction churn when eviction threshold lowered to 30% free (we saw cache thrash for multi-turn sessions).

Experiment design recap:
- Cohort-sampler: assigns incoming requests to cohorts by approximate token-length and model-version compat; within cohort we use a FIFO queue with adaptive delay window (max delay = 12ms).
- Microbatch sizing: target microbatch of 32, fallback to 8/4 when delay window expires.
- KV cache eviction: lowered free buffer target from 45% -> 30% to force earlier evictions and increase effective batch density (config: kv.eviction.target_free_ratio=0.30).
- Workload: 12k QPS synthetic split across three profiles: short chat (<=64 tokens) 60%, medium (65-512) 30%, long (513-2048) 10%.
- Hardware: NVLink A750-like cluster (8-GPU shard), runtime kernel branch: cohort-sampler-v2 (PR above).

Observations and metrics (detailed):
- Token-cost reduction: median tokens/GPU decreased from 1.02M -> 0.90M per minute across runs.
- Latency percentiles (medium profile): median 130ms -> 118ms, p95 210ms -> 205ms, p99 450ms -> 530ms (regression).
- Long profile behavior: p95/p99 unchanged for single-turn flows, but multi-turn long sessions saw p99 bursts up to 1.4x baseline when eviction churn occurred.
- Microbatch distribution: 52% of batches were size >= 24, 26% were 8-23, 22% were <=7 — the small-batch tail correlated with cohort fragmentation during traffic spikes.
- KV eviction churn: when eviction.target_free_ratio=0.30, eviction events increased 3.7x vs baseline. Eviction latency added 30-70ms in the critical path for affected requests (measured via trace hooks).

Hypotheses tested and result summary:
1) Hypothesis: lowering eviction target improves batching density and reduces cost without harming tail latency.
   - Result: false at current config. Lowering target increased cache thrash for sessions with repeated prefixes; tail latency amplified.

2) Hypothesis: increasing adaptive delay window to 20ms would allow small cohorts to accumulate and reduce small-batch frequency.
   - Result: partially true. Small-batch frequency dropped from 22% -> 12%, p99 improved by ~6% but median latency increased slightly during spikes due to queuing.

3) Hypothesis: cohort fingerprinting that includes session-id affinity reduces fragmentation without sacrificing throughput.
   - Result: promising in limited replay tests (replayed production traces). Implementation complexity higher — interacts with routing/fallback policies.

Actionable findings (what to change):
- Revert kv.eviction.target_free_ratio to 0.40 for the next staging rollout. 0.30 introduced too much churn. Owner: Miguel Torres. (JIRA-RT-1468)
- Prototype session-affinity flag in cohort-sampler (cohort.sampler.session_affinity=true) and run a controlled A/B on 10% of traffic. Owner: Jordan Liu. Target: roll out test by 2029-10-10.
- Add eviction-metric annotation in traces so we can correlate eviction events to token lat spikes more precisely (trace tag: kv.evicted=true). Owner: Priya Das.
- Tune adaptive delay window to 16ms for production-env test (balance between microbatch growth and queuing latency). Owner: Evan Kim.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Is there a smarter eviction strategy that prefers prefix-preserving evictions for multi-turn sessions? We should evaluate an LRU variant that weights by recent-turn frequency. (Research: evaluate cost vs hit-rate tradeoff.)
- How will session-affinity interact with cross-region failover and short TTL routing metadata? Need SRE/infra input.
- What is acceptable median increase to get p99 improvement? Product SLA guidance needed — ask Product (Matt S.) for p99 absolute target for multi-turn conversational flows.

Short-term playbook for next week:
1) Roll kv.eviction.target_free_ratio back to 0.40 in staging by 2029-10-04 and re-run mixed-workload replay. (Miguel)
2) Land trace tags and dashboard panels for eviction events + correlated tail-latency heatmap (Priya + Observability). Dashboard: /dashboards/eviction-latency-heatmap (Confluence link above).
3) Begin dev on session-affinity prototype behind feature-flag and run a 10% A/B (Jordan + Evan). Aim to end A/B by 2029-10-14.
4) Short retro with oncall after rollout to capture any unexpected degradation vectors. (All)

Notes from triage meeting 2029-10-01:
- SRE flagged intermittent GPU saturation where small batch packing increased kernel launch count (cost of extra launches > saving from packing in certain shapes). We need a cost model that includes kernel launch overhead per microbatch. (Action: Evan to add per-launch overhead metric to the runtime profiler.)
- Product asked whether prioritizing medium-length requests for batching (i.e., soft-priority bins) would reduce p99 without hurting short chat latency. Preliminary sim suggests yes, but it increases scheduler complexity.

Appendix: quick config snippets and experiment IDs
- Experiment: cohort-sampler-v2-run-2029-09-29 (replay-id: rpl-20290929-72)
- Key runtime flags used:
  --cohort.sampler.strategy=length+compat
  --cohort.sampler.max_delay_ms=12
  --batch.target_microbatch=32
  --kv.eviction.target_free_ratio=0.30

- Traces to inspect (examples):
  trace-2029-09-30-23:07:33-dd2a (contains eviction spike correlated to p99 burst)
  trace-2029-09-29-10:12:01-9b7c (good run, high packing efficiency)

Final thought (lane-level):
The cohort-sampler idea is sound — it improves packing and median token-cost for common workloads. But we were too aggressive on cache pressure. Next run should prioritize tail-latency protection (gentle eviction thresholds + session affinity) and instrument more fine-grained kernel-launch overhead metrics so we can quantify the tradeoffs.

Drafted-by: Asha Patel (notes consolidated from triage + experiment logs).
Reviewers: Miguel, Jordan, Priya.
